column1: # OWASP ZAP baseline — false-positive allowlist (sub-phase 1.8).
# Format (TAB-separated, 3 columns, read by ZAP):
#   <pluginId> <WARN|IGNORE|FAIL> <reason>
#   <pluginId> OUTOFSCOPE <URL regex, anchored ^…$>
# The scan is blocking (Hardening H1): any alert of Low risk or above that is
# not excused here fails the nightly run. Every entry carries its reason;
# tests/guards/security-scan-deferral.test.ts refuses one without. An
# OUTOFSCOPE line's third column is the regex, so its reason is the comment
# block directly above it. Prefer OUTOFSCOPE to IGNORE: it excuses one rule on
# the named URLs only, and the rule still fails anywhere else. An IGNORE
# silences a pluginId at EVERY risk level, so .zap/assert-no-high-risk.mjs
# reads the ignored alerts too: a High is fixed, never listed here. The IGNORE
# entries are adapted from inflect-compliance `.zap/rules.tsv` at
# 5528464fc54a8681956f3b9ce23ca9c075f0420e, with Islestone reasons.

column3: Absence of Anti-CSRF Tokens: NextAuth v4 uses a double-submit CSRF cookie and token that ZAP cannot see as a form field; the credentials callback refuses a request without it.
Information Disclosure - Suspicious Comments: matches comments in framework-generated Next.js chunks, which carry no secrets.
Modern Web Application: informational (the app is JavaScript-driven), not a finding.

CSP: style-src keeps unsafe-inline by design (a style nonce would make browsers ignore it for style attributes the UI emits) and img-src/connect-src allow the https: scheme for OAuth avatars and Sentry; script-src stays nonce + strict-dynamic with no unsafe-inline (src/lib/security/csp.ts).

column1: # 10044 Big Redirect, out of scope on exactly the two redirects a Next.js
# server component makes for a signed-in person: `/` (src/app/page.tsx) and
# the workspace picker's single-destination case (src/app/tenants/page.tsx).
# App Router's redirect() answers 307 with the streamed root-layout shell
# (about 105 KB) for the client router. Evidence (2026-11-26, this scan run
# locally, signed in): both bodies hold the public shell and the
# NEXT_REDIRECT flight entry naming the Location already sent, and no session
# data (not the person's email or name, no workspace but the Location's). A
# signed-out request gets the middleware's bodyless redirect instead.
